{{short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}} {{Infobox constituency |name = Cotabato's 1st congressional district |parl_name = [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |image = |caption = |image2 = Cotabato in Philippines.svg |caption2 = Location of Cotabato within the [[Philippines]] |district_label = Province |district = [[Cotabato]] |region_label = Region |region = [[Soccsksargen]] |population = 403,870 (2024){{Cite web |date=September 12, 2025 |title=Statistical Tables for the Press Release on Legislative District (2024 POPCEN)_0 |url=https://psa.gov.ph/system/files/phcd/Statistical%20Tables%20for%20the%20Press%20Release%20on%20Legislative%20District%20%282024%20POPCEN%29_0.xlsx |access-date=October 24, 2025 |publisher=[[Philippine Statistics Authority]]}} |electorate = 246,037 (2025){{cite web |title=Data on the Total Number Established and Clustered Precincts, Registered Voters and Voting Centers |url=https://comelec.gov.ph/php-tpls-attachments/2025NLE/Statistics/CONSOLIDATED_2025_Number_Of_Registered_Voters.pdf |website=Commission on Elections|accessdate=May 17, 2025}} |area = {{convert|2420.58|sqkm|sqmi|abbr=on}} |towns = {{Collapsible list | titlestyle = font-weight:normal;text-align:left;background-color:WhiteSmoke; | title = 6 [[Local government in the Philippines|LGU]]s | '''Municipalities''' | [[Alamada]] | [[Aleosan]] | [[Libungan]] | [[Midsayap]] | [[Pigcawayan]] | [[Pikit]] }} |year = 1987 |members_label = Representative |members = [[Edwin Cruzado]] |blank1_name = Political party |blank1_info = {{Color box|{{party color|Lakas–CMD}}|border=darkgray}} [[Lakas–CMD]] |blank2_name = Congressional bloc |blank2_info = Majority }} '''Cotabato's 1st congressional district''' is one of the three [[congressional districts of the Philippines]] in the province of [[Cotabato]]. It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] since 1987.{{cite web |url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=February 28, 2021 |archive-date=March 16, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316064243/http://congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |url-status=dead }} The district covers western Cotabato, bordered on three sides by the province of [[Maguindanao]] and which, since 2019, contains several [[Special geographic area of Bangsamoro|exclaves of the Bangsamoro autonomous region]]. It consists of the municipalities of [[Alamada]], [[Aleosan]], [[Libungan]], [[Midsayap]], [[Pigcawayan]] and [[Pikit]].{{cite web|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/2012/09/14/republic-act-no-10177/ |title=Republic Act No. 10177 |date=14 September 2012 |publisher=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)]] |accessdate=February 28, 2021}} Prior to redistricting in 2012, the district also included the municipalities of [[Banisilan]], [[Carmen, Cotabato|Carmen]] and [[Kabacan]].{{cite web|url=https://www.chanrobles.com/ordinance.htm |title=The 1987 Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines |publisher=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library |accessdate=February 28, 2021}} It is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Edwin Cruzado]] of the [[Lakas–CMD]].{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=February 28, 2021}} ==Representation history== {| class=wikitable |- ! rowspan="2" | # ! rowspan="2" colspan=2 | Image ! rowspan="2" | Member ! colspan=2 | Term of office ! rowspan="2" | Congress ! rowspan="2" | Party ! rowspan="2" | Electoral history ! rowspan="2" | Constituent
